mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day forward returns despite sustained high FEDFUNDS, or 12-month rolling IC > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5% while PAYEMS increases by at least 2% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative despite the labor indicators meeting the trigger, or the correlation falls below 0.3 in a 30-day rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in personal consumption expenditures ( proxy: GDPC1 ) coinciding with a drop in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a shift from inventory-driven to demand-driven economic growth, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 month-over-month increase exceeds 4% while INDPRO month-over-month decrease exceeds 2%
regime_hint: transition from inventory accumulation to consumption-led growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward return is negative when the signal is active, or IC < -0.1 over the 5-day window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) over three consecutive months suggests supply-side constraints, lowering growth expectations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO contracting for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite INDPRO contraction, or 12-month rolling IC remains above 0.0.

mechanism_narrative: When the US inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the market anticipates a near-term rate hike, which compresses discount rates and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day forward returns during the inflation spike, or 12-month rolling IC remains above 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in job openings (proxy: not available in provided catalog - so skip interaction) is not possible; instead, a sharp rise in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% triggers a risk-off reaction, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite UNRATE falling below 4%, or IC > 0.2 in the risk-off regime.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales ( proxy: not available - use HOUST as proxy for consumer activity ) and increasing housing starts (HOUST) signal a recovery in consumer and builder confidence, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by at least 5% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are flat or negative despite the indicated consumer and housing activity.

mechanism_narrative: During a supply shock (e.g., RSAFS < 300 billion for two months), manufacturing activity weakens and the S&P 500 anticipates slower growth, resulting in negative forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS remains below 300 billion for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite sustained weakness in manufacturing demand (RSAFS).
